name: go-streams-event-time-watermarks-across-baf4
instr:
go-streams cannot carry timestamped records and watermarks safely through its existing Flow composition model. Add event-time support without changing unconfigured transformation, aggregation, batching, ordering, terminal emission, completion, or ordinary Flow channel behavior.

Every event-time flow must emit monotonic progress, suppress regressions, and handle equal watermarks idempotently without duplicating buffered output. `flow.NewMap`, `flow.NewFilter`, `flow.NewFlatMap`, `flow.NewPassThrough`, `flow.NewFold`, `flow.NewReduce`, `flow.NewBatch`, `flow.NewKeyed`, `flow.NewTumblingWindow`, `flow.NewSlidingWindow`, and `flow.NewSessionWindow` must preserve event-time identity and existing semantics. Progress must follow earlier and eligible output. It must wait for every active key. Session output must close once on event-time inactivity when timers compete.

The listed pointer-receiver methods accept `config` and return event-time-capable flows. Batch and window boundaries emit eligible records once before progress when size, timers, watermarks, or closure compete, with no empty terminal batches. FlatMap output must be fully observable before its watermark.

Split, FanOut, RoundRobin, Merge, ZipWith, Via, and To must preserve routing and causal progress. Branches advance after earlier data; joins cannot pass the least-progressed open input; watermarks are not data. Consumers receive data before progress and finish after output closes.
